title: Solve multiplication and division word problems, interpreting the remainder

lesson.title: What Do We Do With the Leftovers?

steps.say: You already know how to divide and say what the remainder means, like twenty-six divided by six is four with two left over. Today we take one more little step: in a real story problem, we have to decide what to do with those leftovers.

Here is the trick. After you divide, stop and picture the story in your head. Ask yourself, can I really leave the leftover behind? If the leftover is a person, or a muffin, or anything that still needs a spot, then you need one more group. Let's try it with a class trip to the aquarium.

Twenty-six students are going, and each van holds six students. Six times four is twenty-four, and twenty-six take away twenty-four leaves two. So twenty-six divided by six is four, remainder two. Four full vans, and two students still standing on the sidewalk.

visual.caption: 4 full vans of 6, with 2 students left over

steps.say: Now the important part. Those two students cannot stay behind, so they need a van of their own. That van is not full, but it still counts. Four vans plus one more van makes five vans. The answer is five, not four.

visual.caption: The fifth van is only half full, but we still need it

steps.say: Two mistakes to watch for. First, writing four vans and forgetting the two children on the sidewalk. Always check that everybody got a seat. Second, choosing multiplying just because you saw the word each. The words each van holds six do not mean multiply. Think about the story: we are putting students into groups of six, so we divide.
So after you divide, always go back and read the question one more time, and ask what the leftover really means in the story.

lesson.answer: Divide first, then look at the leftover: if it still needs a spot, add one more group.

practice.question: For the school bake sale in Burnaby, you baked fifty blueberry muffins. Each box holds eight muffins. How many boxes do you need so that every single muffin is packed? Try drawing the boxes yourself.
practice.answer: Seven boxes. Fifty divided by eight is six, remainder two. Six full boxes hold forty-eight muffins, and the last two muffins still need a box, so six plus one is seven.
